learning: Hypotheses: (1) lower yaw inertia reduces bend line loss; (2) the oval finish rate holds at or above 0.75; (3) if line loss stays at 2.0 with lower mass, the limit is control response or wheel saturation, not geometry, and further geometry search should stop. If the score falls below 291.9, the next design should return to mass 0.6 kg with the iteration-4 geometry.
notes: Iteration-4 controller and layout with mass 0.6 to 0.5 kg as the only change. Measurements match the Builder's request per track, so the oval finish rate, completion_time, line loss and steering oscillation can be compared directly with iteration 4.
rationale: The Builder's geometry is the iteration-4 layout (best score 291.9) with mass changed from 0.6 to 0.5 kg. Iteration 4 is the only design where the oval finished runs (15 of 20). Iterations 5 (60 mm span, 73.6), 6 (16 mm footprint, 83.5) and 7 (wheel_track 0.10 m, 83.5) all lost the oval finishes (0 of 20) and kept line_loss_events at 2.0 on the s-bend and slalom. Iteration 7 is the clearest case: the narrower track did not clear line loss, and max_error rose to 0.065 to 0.070, so my rule to return wheel_track to 0.12 m applies. The Builder's geometry already restores 0.12 m. The mass change alone is the only variable I am asked to test, so I keep the iteration-4 controller exactly: base_speed 1.4, kp 4.0, ki 0.1, kd 0.4, last_direction, weights [-1, -0.5, 0, 0.5, 1]. kd 0.4 is kept because it brought steering_oscillation down to 0.16 on the oval at iteration 4. Lower mass reduces yaw inertia, so the same kp gives a quicker turn; I do not retune gains, so any change in score can be attributed to mass. Expected result: the oval finish rate holds at or above 0.75 and line_loss_events on the bends may fall. This is a prediction, not a measured result. Risk: lighter mass changes traction and speed response, so the oval finish rate and steering_oscillation are the watch points.
